pages.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
retelling: One evening Jesus and his friends got into a boat to cross the lake. Jesus lay down at the back of the boat, on a cushion, and fell asleep.
Then a big storm came. The wind blew hard and the waves splashed into the boat. His friends were frightened.
“Teacher, help!” they cried. “The boat is filling with water!”
Jesus woke up. He spoke to the wind and the waves. “Quiet!” he said. “Be still!”
At once the wind stopped, and the lake was calm.
Jesus asked his friends, “Why are you so afraid?” They looked at one another. “Who is this?” they asked. “Even the wind and the waves do what he says!”
pages.message: Jesus is with us in every storm. Even the wind and the waves listen to him.

questions.q: Where was Jesus when the storm came?
questions.a: Asleep at the back of the boat.

questions.q: What did Jesus say to the wind and the waves?
questions.a: He told them to be quiet and still.

questions.q: When you feel scared, what can you remember about Jesus?
questions.a: He is with us, and even the wind and the waves obey him. Let the child say it in their own words.

pages.try_this: Make a rain sound with your fingers on the table, getting louder. Then say “Be still!” together and stop. Notice how quiet it gets.

pages.title: David and the Giant
retelling: David was a shepherd boy. He looked after his father's sheep, and he trusted God to keep him safe.
One day David took some food to his big brothers, who were soldiers. The soldiers were scared. A giant called Goliath shouted at them every day, and nobody dared to fight him.
“I will fight him,” said David. “God helped me when a lion and a bear came after my sheep. God will help me now.”
The king let David try on his armour. But David was not used to it, so he took it off. He picked up his stick and his sling, and he chose five smooth stones from the stream.
“You have a sword and a spear,” David called to Goliath. “But I come in the name of the LORD.”
David swung his sling. The stone flew through the air, and Goliath fell down. The soldiers of Israel gave a great shout. Everyone could see that God had helped David.
pages.message: God is bigger than any giant. When we trust God, we do not have to be afraid.

questions.q: Who helped David when the lion and the bear came?
questions.a: God did. David said so.

questions.q: What did David take to meet Goliath?
questions.a: A stick, a sling and five smooth stones. He left the armour behind.

questions.q: What makes you feel afraid? What could you say to God about it?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk, then pray together.

pages.try_this: Find five smooth stones or draw five on paper. Say the memory verse each time you pick one up.

pages.title: Noah and the Big Boat
retelling: God told Noah to build a big boat. The boat was called an ark. Noah did just what God said.
Noah and his family went into the ark. The animals came too, two by two. Then God himself shut the door.
The rain fell for forty days. Water covered the whole earth. But the ark floated on top, and God kept everyone inside safe.
God remembered Noah. He sent a wind, and the water went down. The ark stopped on top of a mountain. But Noah still had to wait.

Noah let a dove fly out of the ark. The dove came back. A week later, Noah sent it out again. This time it came back with a fresh leaf from an olive tree. A week later, Noah sent it out once more. The dove did not come back.
Even then, Noah did not rush out. He waited for God to say it was time. They had been in the ark for about a year.
At last the ground was dry. “Come out of the ark!” said God. Out came Noah, his family and all the animals.
Then God made a promise. He would never flood the whole earth again. He put a rainbow in the clouds to show it.
pages.message: God keeps us safe, and God keeps his promises. When we wait for God, he knows the right time.

questions.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
questions.a: A leaf from an olive tree. It showed that the water was going down.

questions.q: What did God promise after the flood?
questions.a: That he would never flood the whole earth again. The rainbow is the sign of his promise.

questions.q: Who looks after you and keeps you safe? How can you say thank you?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name the people who care for them, then thank God together for looking after us.

pages.try_this: Draw a rainbow with as many colours as you can. Line up some toy animals two by two, and say together, “God keeps his promises.”

pages.title: Baby Moses in the Basket
retelling: A baby boy was born. His mother loved him very much. She kept him hidden for three months, so that he would be safe.
Soon she could not hide him any longer. So she made a basket and covered it with tar. She put the baby inside and set the basket in the reeds by the river.
The baby's sister waited nearby and kept watch.
Then a princess came down to the river. She was the king's daughter. She noticed the basket and told her maid to bring it.
The princess opened the basket. The baby was crying! She felt sorry for him.
His sister came over. “Shall I find a nurse for the baby?” she asked. “Yes, go,” said the princess.
The girl hurried off and came back with her own mother! “Please take care of this baby for me,” said the princess. “I will pay you.” So the mother looked after her own baby.
When the boy was older, he became the princess's son. She called him Moses, because she had pulled him from the river.
pages.message: God looks after us, even when things feel scary. He has a plan for every child.

questions.q: Who kept watch over the basket?
questions.a: His sister.

questions.q: Who found the basket and felt sorry for the baby?
questions.a: The king's daughter, a princess.

questions.q: Who helps you when you need help? How could you thank them?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name some helpers, then remind them that God is our help too, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Make a little basket from paper or a small box. Put a toy baby inside, hide it, and let your child find it and say, “Safe!”

pages.title: The Birth of Jesus
retelling: Mary and Joseph lived in Nazareth. An angel came to Mary. “You will have a baby,” he said. “He will be the Son of God.” Mary said, “I am the Lord's servant.” An angel also told Joseph, in a dream, to call the baby Jesus.
Then the Roman ruler, Caesar Augustus, ordered everyone to be counted in their family's own town. So Joseph and Mary travelled to Bethlehem, where Joseph's family came from.
While they were there, Mary's baby was born. She wrapped him in cloths and put him down in a manger, a feeding box for animals.
That night, shepherds were out in the fields, watching their sheep. Suddenly an angel appeared, and a bright light shone around them. The shepherds were frightened.
“Don't be afraid!” said the angel. “I have wonderful news for everyone. Today your Savior is born in Bethlehem. He is Christ the Lord. You will find the baby in cloths, in a manger.”
Then a huge crowd of angels appeared. They praised God and spoke of peace on earth.
When the angels had gone, the shepherds said, “Let's go to Bethlehem!” They rushed there and found the baby with Mary and Joseph, just as the angel had said.
The shepherds told everyone the good news. Mary kept all these things safe in her heart.
pages.message: Jesus is God's gift to the whole world. God loves us so much that he sent his Son to save us.

questions.q: Why did Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem?
questions.a: The ruler, Caesar Augustus, ordered everyone to be counted in their own family's town, and Joseph's family came from Bethlehem.

questions.q: What sign did the angel give the shepherds?
questions.a: They would find a baby in cloths, in a manger.

questions.q: The shepherds told everyone the good news. What good news about Jesus could you tell someone this week?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child think of one person, and a grown-up can help them say it, write it or draw it.

pages.try_this: Use a small box as a manger and a doll or toy as the baby. Let the shepherds hurry over to find him, then tell the good news.

pages.title: The Boy with the Lunch
retelling: One day a huge crowd followed Jesus across the Sea of Galilee. They had seen him make sick people well.
Jesus looked at all the people and asked his friend Philip where they could buy enough bread. Jesus already knew what he was going to do. He was testing Philip.
Philip said that two hundred coins would not be enough. Not even a small piece for each person!
Then Andrew, another friend of Jesus, spoke up. He had found a boy. The boy had just five small loaves of barley bread and two fish. “But how far will that go among so many people?” Andrew asked.
“Tell everyone to sit down,” said Jesus. There was lots of grass there, and about five thousand men sat down.
Jesus took the bread and the fish. He thanked God for them, and he shared them out. Everyone ate as much as they liked!
When they were all full, Jesus told his friends to collect what was left, so that none of it would go to waste. They filled twelve baskets.
The people saw what Jesus had done. They said he must be the Prophet who was coming.
pages.message: Jesus can do big things with the little we share. When we give what we have, God can make it enough.

questions.q: What food did the boy have?
questions.a: Five small loaves of barley bread and two fish.

questions.q: How much food was left over at the end?
questions.a: Twelve baskets full of pieces. Jesus told his friends to gather them so that nothing was wasted.

questions.q: The boy had only a little, and Jesus used it for everyone. What small thing could you share with others?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. It might be a toy, a snack, a kind word or some time. Help the child pick one thing to share this week.

pages.try_this: Share a snack. Cut a little fruit or bread into small pieces, thank God for it together, then hand the pieces round.

pages.title: Zacchaeus in the Tree
retelling: Jesus was walking through Jericho, and a big crowd had gathered. A wealthy man called Zacchaeus lived there. He was in charge of the tax collectors.
Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus. But he was short, and he could not see past the crowd. So he ran ahead of everyone and scrambled up a sycamore tree.
When Jesus reached the tree, he looked up. “Zacchaeus!” he said. “Come down quickly. I must be your guest today.”
Zacchaeus came down at once and welcomed him gladly. But everyone who saw it began to complain. Jesus was staying with a sinner, they said.
Then Zacchaeus stood up and spoke to the Lord. He would give half of everything he owned to the poor. If he had cheated anyone, he would repay four times as much.
Jesus said that salvation had come to that house, because Zacchaeus was a son of Abraham too. Jesus had come, he said, to look for lost people and to save them.
pages.message: Jesus loves everyone, even people that others leave out. When we meet Jesus, we want to put right what we did wrong.

questions.q: Why did Zacchaeus climb a tree?
questions.a: He was too short to see past the crowd, and he wanted to see Jesus.

questions.q: What did Zacchaeus promise to do?
questions.a: Give half of what he owned to the poor, and pay back four times as much to anyone he had cheated.

questions.q: Jesus chose to visit Zacchaeus, even though the crowd grumbled. Is there someone who is often left out at school or near your home? What could you do?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Help the young person think of one small, safe step, such as saying hello or sitting with that person, and pray for them together.

pages.try_this: Draw what Zacchaeus saw from the branch. Then write one thing you could give away or put right this week, and tell someone.

pages.title: God Makes the World
retelling: In the beginning, the world was dark and empty. Then God spoke. “Let there be light!” said God. And the light shone.
God looked at the light. It was good! He named the light Day, and he named the dark Night. That was the first day.
God made everything just by speaking. On the second day, he made the big blue sky. On the third day, he made dry land and seas. Then he made plants and fruit trees.
On the fourth day, God made the sun, the moon and the stars. They shine in the sky.
On the fifth day, God made fish for the sea and birds for the sky. God blessed them.
On the sixth day, God made animals to live on the land. Last of all, God made people. He made a man and a woman, and he made them like himself.
God looked at everything he had made. It was very good!
On the seventh day, God rested. God blessed that day and made it special.
pages.message: God made the whole world, and he made you. Everything God makes is good.

questions.q: How did God make the world?
questions.a: He made everything just by speaking.

questions.q: What did God do on the seventh day?
questions.a: He rested, and he made that day special.

questions.q: What is your favourite thing that God made? Can you say thank you to God for it?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child choose, then thank God together for that one thing.

pages.try_this: Go outside and find something God made: a leaf, a stone or a feather. Look at it closely, then say together, “Thank you, God, for making this!”
pages.doctrine_note: Christians read the six days of Genesis 1 in different ways, so this page tells only what the text says and takes no side.

pages.title: Jonah and the Big Fish
retelling: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, a big city. The people there were doing bad things, and God wanted Jonah to warn them.
But Jonah did not want to go. He ran away from God! He got on a ship that sailed the other way.
Then God sent a big wind. The waves rose high, and the ship shook. The sailors were scared. But Jonah was fast asleep.
The sailors found out that Jonah was running from God. “It is my fault,” said Jonah. “Put me in the sea, and the storm will stop.”
The sailors rowed and rowed, but the storm got worse. At last they put Jonah into the sea. At once the sea was calm.
Then God sent a big fish. The fish swallowed Jonah! Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
Jonah prayed to God from inside the fish. He said thank you for hearing him. Then God told the fish to put Jonah on dry land.
God spoke to Jonah again. “Go to Nineveh,” he said. This time Jonah went. The people there listened. They were sorry, and God was kind to them.
pages.message: We cannot run away from God. He is with us everywhere, and he gives us another chance.

questions.q: What did Jonah do when God told him to go to Nineveh?
questions.a: He ran away. He got on a ship that sailed the other way.

questions.q: What did Jonah do inside the big fish?
questions.a: He prayed, and God heard him. Then the fish put him on dry land.

questions.q: Is there something you do not want to do? What could you tell God about it?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child say it in their own words. A grown-up can remind them that God still loves us and gives us another chance.

pages.try_this: Make a big fish from paper, with a wide mouth. Put a small paper Jonah inside, then take him out and say, “God gives second chances!”

pages.title: Daniel and the Lions
retelling: Daniel loved God. Three times every day, he knelt by his window and prayed. He said thank you to God.
Daniel worked for the king, and he did his work well. The king liked Daniel very much. But some other men were jealous.
These men tricked the king. For thirty days, no one could pray to anyone but the king. If they did, they would be put in a den of lions.
Daniel heard about the new rule. But he still prayed to God, just as before.
The king was sad, but the rule could not be changed. So Daniel was put in the den with the lions. A big stone covered the door. “May your God keep you safe,” said the king.
All night, the king could not sleep. At first light he hurried to the den. “Daniel!” he called. “Did your God keep you safe?”
“Yes!” said Daniel. “God sent his angel. He shut the lions’ mouths, so they could not hurt me.”
The king was so happy! Daniel came out of the den. He did not have one scratch, because he trusted God.
Then the king wrote to everyone in his land. He said that Daniel’s God is the living God.
pages.message: Daniel kept praying to God, even when it was hard. God was with him and took care of him.

questions.q: What did Daniel do three times every day?
questions.a: He prayed to God and thanked him.

questions.q: Who shut the lions’ mouths?
questions.a: God did. He sent his angel to keep Daniel safe.

questions.q: Can you talk to God at any time? What would you like to say to him today?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. We can pray anywhere, and God hears us. Let the child say a short prayer, or say one together.

pages.try_this: Sit by a window and say a short prayer, just like Daniel. Say thank you to God for three things, and count them on your fingers.

pages.title: Samuel Hears God
retelling: Samuel was a boy who helped Eli, an old priest, in God’s house. In those days, people did not often hear from God.
One night Samuel was lying down when a voice called his name. “Here I am!” he said. He ran to Eli. “You called me,” he said.
“I did not call you,” said Eli. “Go back to bed.” So Samuel lay down again. Then it happened a second time, and a third time.
Samuel had never heard God speak before, so he did not know who was calling. But now Eli understood. He told Samuel what to say if the voice came again: “Speak, LORD. I am listening.”
This time, the LORD himself was there. “Samuel! Samuel!” he called. “Speak, LORD,” said Samuel. “I am listening.”
Then God gave Samuel his message. It was a sad message about Eli’s family. Eli’s sons had done wrong, and Eli had not stopped them.
In the morning, Samuel was scared to tell Eli. But Eli asked him to say everything, and Samuel hid nothing. Eli said that the LORD must do what is best.
God was with Samuel as he grew up. Everything Samuel said came true. All Israel knew that Samuel spoke for God. He was a prophet, someone who tells people what God says.
pages.message: Hearing God call is not the same as hearing his message. The message came when Samuel said, “I am listening.” God speaks to us when we listen.

questions.q: Who did Samuel think was calling him, and who helped him understand?
questions.a: He thought it was Eli. Eli worked out that God was calling, and he told Samuel what to say.

questions.q: What did Samuel say when the LORD called again, and what happened then?
questions.a: He said that he was listening. Then God gave him the message.

questions.q: Is there a quiet time in your day when you could stop and listen to God?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. It could be bedtime, or a walk. A grown-up can help the child choose a time, then pray together, “Speak, LORD, I am listening.”

pages.try_this: Sit quietly for one whole minute. Listen to every sound around you. Then say together, “Speak, LORD, I am listening,” and be still for a moment.

pages.title: Moses and the Burning Bush
retelling: Moses looked after sheep for his father-in-law. One day he led them far into the desert, to Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he saw a strange sight. A bush was on fire, but it did not burn up! “I must go and look,” said Moses.
God called to him from the bush. “Moses! Moses!” “Here I am,” said Moses.
“Come no closer,” said God. “Take off your sandals. This ground is holy.” Moses covered his face. He did not dare to look at God.
God said that he was the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He had seen how his people suffered as slaves in Egypt, and he had heard them cry out. Now he was coming to rescue them.
God was sending Moses to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to lead his people out.
But Moses was worried. “Who am I to do this?” he asked. He said that he was slow of speech and not good with words.
God did not choose someone else. He said, “I will be with you.” He promised to help Moses speak, and to teach him what to say.
God warned Moses that Pharaoh would not let the people go at first. But God would show his great power, and then they would be free.
pages.message: God can use anyone, even someone who feels small or weak. He does not need us to be perfect. He goes with us.

questions.q: What was strange about the bush?
questions.a: It was on fire, but it did not burn up.

questions.q: Moses said he was slow of speech. What did God promise him?
questions.a: God promised to be with him, to help him speak and to teach him what to say.

questions.q: Is there something you feel too small or too shy to do? What do you think God would say to you?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk. A grown-up can remind them that God was with Moses and is with us too, then pray together.

pages.try_this: Take off your shoes for a moment and stand quietly. Think about how great God is. Then draw a bush with flames of red, orange and yellow.

pages.title: Crossing the Red Sea
retelling: God’s people, the Israelites, had left Egypt. Moses led them, and God went with them. But then Pharaoh changed his mind.
Pharaoh sent his army after them, with hundreds of chariots. The Israelites were camping beside the sea when they saw the army coming.
The sea was in front of them, and the army was behind them. They were terrified! They cried out to God for help.
“Do not be afraid,” Moses told the people. “Watch and see what God does today. He will fight for you.”
God told Moses to hold out his hand over the sea. The cloud that led the people moved behind them, between them and the army. It kept the two camps apart all night.
All night a strong wind blew, and the sea was pushed back. A path of dry ground appeared, with a wall of water on each side!
The Israelites walked across. The ground under their feet was dry. God had made a way when there was no way.
When all the Israelites were across, God told Moses to stretch out his hand again. The water came back, and Israel was safe.
The people saw God’s great power. They trusted God, and they trusted his servant Moses.
pages.message: God can make a way when there seems to be no way. We do not need to be afraid. We can trust him.

questions.q: Why were the Israelites so afraid?
questions.a: The sea was in front of them, and Pharaoh’s army was coming up behind them.

questions.q: How did God open a way through the sea?
questions.a: Moses held out his hand, and God sent a strong wind all night. It pushed the water back, and the people walked across on dry ground.

questions.q: Has there been a time when you could not see a way out? Who could pray with you about it?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child tell what they remember. A grown-up can remind them that God made a way for Israel and still helps us today.

pages.try_this: Lay two long blue cloths on the floor with a path between them. Walk down the path together, saying, “God makes a way!”

pages.title: The Walls of Jericho
retelling: Jericho was a city with high walls. Its gates were shut tight, because the Israelites were near.
God spoke to Joshua, the leader of Israel. He said that he had already given Jericho to Joshua. Then he told Joshua a very strange plan.
Every day for six days, the soldiers were to march around the city once. Seven priests would walk in front, blowing trumpets made of rams’ horns. The ark, God’s special box, came behind them.
The people had to stay silent. Joshua told them not to say one word until it was time to shout.
So the soldiers marched around Jericho once, with the horns sounding. Then they went back to camp. This went on for six days.
On day seven, the army was up early. This time, they marched around the city seven times.
Then the priests blew one long blast. “Shout!” said Joshua. “God has given you this city!”
The people shouted as loudly as they could. The wall came tumbling down! The Israelites went into Jericho.
Rahab, a woman in Jericho, had once hidden two of Joshua’s spies. Joshua kept the promise made to her. His men brought Rahab and her family out safely, and they lived among God’s people.
pages.message: God’s plans may look strange, but they work. We trust God and do what he says. Then he does what we cannot do.

questions.q: What did the people have to do while they marched?
questions.a: They had to stay completely silent. Only the priests’ horns made a sound.

questions.q: What happened on the seventh day?
questions.a: They marched around the city seven times. Then the priests blew a long blast, the people shouted and the wall fell down.

questions.q: Is there something you find hard to do because you cannot see how it will work out? How could you trust God with it?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. A grown-up can help them think of one way to trust God this week, then pray together.

pages.try_this: March around a table together, once a day for six days, in silence. On day seven, march seven times, then shout and knock down a tower of blocks.

pages.title: The Son Who Came Home
retelling: There was a man with two sons. The younger son asked for his share of the money. Then he went far away.
He wasted everything he had. A famine came, and he took a job feeding pigs. He was so hungry that he wanted the pigs' food.
At last he decided to go home and say sorry.
The son was still far from home when his father saw him coming. The father ran to him, hugged him and kissed him. “Father, I did wrong to God and to you,” said the son.
He called to his servants. “Bring the best robe and a ring! Let's have a feast! My son was lost, and now he is found!”
The older son was out in the field. When he heard about the party, he got angry and stayed outside. His father went out and begged him. “I worked for you,” he said, “but I never got a party!”
“Son, you are with me every day,” said the father. “All I have is yours. But we had to celebrate! Your brother was lost, and now he is found!”
Jesus does not say if the older son went in. Jesus also told about a lost sheep and a lost coin. Heaven is full of joy when one lost person is found.
pages.message: God is like the father who ran to welcome his son home. Heaven is full of joy when one lost person is found. There is a place at the party for everyone.

questions.q: What job did the younger son take when his money was gone?
questions.a: He fed pigs, and he was so hungry that he wanted to eat their food.

questions.q: What did the father do when he saw his son far away?
questions.a: He ran to his son, hugged him and kissed him. Then he gave him a robe and a ring, and held a feast.

questions.q: Have you ever done something wrong and then said sorry? How did it feel to be forgiven?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk. A grown-up can share a time they were forgiven, and remind the child that God is always ready to welcome us home.

pages.try_this: Act out the story. One person comes home from far away, and the others run to hug them. Then share a special snack and say together, “Lost and found!”

pages.title: Jesus Walks on the Water
retelling: Jesus sent his friends ahead of him in a boat. Then he went up a mountain to pray alone.
That night the boat was far from land. The wind was blowing hard against it, and the waves tossed it about.
Very late, Jesus came toward the boat. He was walking on the lake! His friends were terrified and thought he was a ghost.
At once Jesus called to them. “Don't be afraid! It is me.”
“Lord, if it really is you,” called Peter, “let me walk to you on the water!”
“Come,” said Jesus. Peter climbed out of the boat. He walked on the water toward Jesus!
But then Peter noticed how strong the wind was. He took his eyes off Jesus and looked at the waves. He was frightened, and he began to sink. “Lord, save me!” he cried.
At once Jesus reached out and caught him. “Why did you doubt?” he asked. The wind stopped as soon as they were in the boat.
His friends worshipped Jesus. “You are truly God's Son!” they said.
pages.message: Keep your eyes on Jesus, not on the wind and waves. If you start to sink, cry out to him. He will catch you!

questions.q: What did Peter do when Jesus said, “Come”?
questions.a: He climbed out of the boat and walked toward Jesus on the water.

questions.q: What happened when Peter looked at the wind and the waves?
questions.a: He was frightened and began to sink. Then he cried out, and Jesus caught him.

questions.q: Peter called out to Jesus when he began to sink. What could you say to Jesus when you feel worried or scared?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child say it in their own words. A grown-up can pray a short prayer together, such as “Jesus, help me!”

pages.try_this: Stand on one foot and look at one spot on the wall. Then look all around and see what happens. Say, “Keep your eyes on Jesus!”

pages.title: Jesus Is Alive!
retelling: Early on Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene walked to the tomb where Jesus was buried. The stone had been moved away. She ran to tell Peter and another friend of Jesus. “Someone has taken the Lord away!” she said.

The two men ran to the tomb. The other man got there first and looked in. Peter went inside and saw the linen cloths. The other man went in too, and he believed. They did not yet understand that the Scriptures said Jesus must rise again.
Mary stayed outside, crying. She looked in and saw two angels dressed in white. “Why are you crying?” they asked. “My Lord is gone,” she answered, “and I cannot find him.”
Then she turned around and saw someone there. She thought he was the gardener. “Sir, if you have moved him, tell me where he is,” she said.
“Mary,” said the man. At once she knew his voice. It was Jesus, alive! “Teacher!” she cried.
Jesus sent her to tell his followers. Mary went to them. “I have seen the Lord!” she announced.
Jesus did not leave right away. For forty days he appeared to his followers again and again, showing them in many ways that he was alive. Then, as they watched, he was lifted up to heaven.
pages.message: Jesus rose from the dead, and he is alive! For forty days he showed his friends that it was true. Then he went up to heaven.

questions.q: Who went to the tomb early on Sunday morning, and what did she find?
questions.a: Mary Magdalene. She found the stone moved away from the entrance.

questions.q: Mary thought the man was the gardener. How did she know it was Jesus?
questions.a: He said her name, “Mary.” Then she turned to him and knew who he was.

questions.q: Mary was full of joy when she saw Jesus alive. Who could you tell this good news to, and how?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the young person choose one person. A grown-up can help them write a note, plan what to say, and pray for that person together.

pages.try_this: Make a card that says “Jesus is alive!” and decorate it. Give it to someone this week, and tell them what Mary told his followers.

pages.title: The Good Samaritan
retelling: An expert in God's law asked Jesus what to do to have eternal life. He said the law tells us to love God and to love our neighbor. But then he asked, “Who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered with a story. A man was walking down the road from Jerusalem to Jericho. Robbers attacked him, beat him and left him half dead.
A priest came along the road. He saw the man and crossed to the far side. Later a Levite, who helped in God's house, did the same.
Then a Samaritan came by. In those days, many Jews and Samaritans did not get along. But when the Samaritan saw the hurt man, his heart went out to him.
He bandaged the man's wounds and poured oil and wine on them. He lifted him onto his own animal and took him to an inn. There he took care of him.
The next day the Samaritan gave the innkeeper two silver coins. “Look after him,” he said. “If it costs more, I will pay you when I come back.”
Jesus asked, “Which of the three men acted like a neighbor to the one who was hurt?” “The one who showed mercy,” the expert answered. “Go and do the same,” said Jesus.
pages.message: Our neighbor is anyone who needs our help, not only our friends. Jesus tells us to show mercy, just as the Samaritan did.

questions.q: Who walked away from the hurt man, and who stopped to help him?
questions.a: A priest and a Levite crossed to the far side of the road. A Samaritan stopped and bandaged the man. He took him to an inn and paid for his care.

questions.q: What did Jesus ask the expert at the end, and what did the expert answer?
questions.a: Jesus asked which of the three men acted like a neighbor to the one who was hurt. The expert answered, “The one who showed mercy.”

questions.q: Is there someone near you, at school or at home, who needs help or a kind word? What could you do?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Help the young person think of one small, safe act of kindness for this week, and pray together that God will give them a caring heart.

pages.try_this: Do one kind thing for someone this week without being asked, such as helping at home or sharing something. Write it down afterwards and thank God.

pages.title: Ruth Stays with Naomi
retelling: Long ago there was a famine in Bethlehem. A man named Elimelech took his wife Naomi and their two sons to live in Moab, a foreign land.
Elimelech died. The sons married two Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth. After about ten years, both sons died too, and Naomi was left alone.
Then Naomi heard that God had given his people food in Judah. She decided to go home, and Ruth and Orpah set out with her.
On the road, Naomi told the young women to go back to their own mothers' homes. They wept and wept. Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye and went back, but Ruth held on to her.
“I will go where you go,” Ruth said. She promised to live where Naomi lived. Naomi's people would be her family now, and she would follow Naomi's God. She would stay until death.
So the two women came to Bethlehem. The whole town was stirred, and Naomi said she had left full but had come home empty. It was the start of the barley harvest.
But God had not forgotten them. Later, Ruth married a kind man named Boaz. Their son Obed became the grandfather of King David. So Ruth, the foreigner from Moab, became David's great-grandmother.
pages.message: No matter who you are or where you come from, God chooses you and has a plan for you. You are valuable, important and loved.

questions.q: Which of the two young women went back home, and which one stayed with Naomi?
questions.a: Orpah went back to her own people. Ruth held on to Naomi and stayed with her.

questions.q: What promise did Ruth make to Naomi?
questions.a: She would go where Naomi went and live where Naomi lived. She would join Naomi's people, follow Naomi's God, and stay with her until death.

questions.q: Ruth was a stranger in Bethlehem, but God had a plan for her. When have you felt like an outsider? What do you want to remember about how God sees you?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the young person talk, and listen. A grown-up can say that God sees each of us as valuable and loved, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Draw a little family tree: Ruth, Obed, Jesse and King David. Then add one more leaf with your own name and the words “Loved by God.”

pages.title: Joseph the Dreamer
retelling: Joseph was one of twelve brothers, and their father Jacob loved him most. His brothers were jealous. Joseph told them his dreams, which seemed to say they would bow down to him. They became angry.
One day they put Joseph in an empty pit and sold him to traders on their way to Egypt. Their father Jacob cried for many days, thinking Joseph was dead.
In Egypt, God was with Joseph. But someone told lies about him, and he ended up in prison. God was with him there too.

Years later, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had dreams nobody could explain. Joseph was brought out of prison, and he said that only God could give the answer. God showed that seven good years would come, then seven years of famine.

Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over all Egypt. Joseph stored up grain. When the hunger came, Joseph's brothers traveled to Egypt to buy food. They bowed low before him, just as in the dreams. They did not know who he was.

At last Joseph could not hold back his tears. “I am Joseph!” he said. His brothers were terrified. But Joseph told them not to blame themselves. God had sent him ahead to save lives. Joseph forgave them. He kissed each of his brothers and cried.
pages.message: God's plan is bigger than ours, even when we do not understand. He uses hard times to get us ready. Joseph forgave his brothers, and we can forgive too.

questions.q: Why were Joseph's brothers so angry with him?
questions.a: Their father loved Joseph most, and Joseph told them dreams that seemed to say they would bow down to him.

questions.q: What did Joseph tell his brothers when he showed them who he was?
questions.a: He told them not to blame themselves, because God had sent him ahead to save lives. Then he forgave them and kissed each one.

questions.q: Joseph went through hard times before God used him. Is something hard happening in your life? What could you say to God about it, and is there someone you need to forgive?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the young person talk, and listen. A grown-up can share a hard time that God used in their own life, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Draw four boxes showing where Joseph lived: the pit, a house in Egypt, the prison and Pharaoh's palace. Write across the top, “God had a plan.”

pages.title: Blind Bartimaeus
retelling: Bartimaeus was blind. He could not see. He sat by the road in Jericho and asked people for money.
One day he heard a big crowd coming. Someone said, “Jesus of Nazareth is here!”
Bartimaeus shouted, “Jesus, please help me!” Some people said, “Be quiet!” But he shouted even louder.
Jesus stopped. He said, “Call him here.” The people said, “Cheer up! Jesus is calling you!”
Bartimaeus threw off his cloak. He jumped up and ran to Jesus.
Jesus asked, “What can I do for you?” Bartimaeus said, “I want to see again.”
Jesus said, “Go. Your faith has healed you.” At once Bartimaeus could see! He followed Jesus down the road.
pages.message: Jesus hears us when we call. He stops for us, and he cares about what we need.

questions.q: What was Bartimaeus's problem?
questions.a: He was blind. He could not see.

questions.q: What did some people tell him to do, and what did he do?
questions.a: They told him to be quiet. He shouted even louder.

questions.q: Bartimaeus kept calling for Jesus. What would you like to ask Jesus? You can talk to him now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk, then pray together.

pages.try_this: Close your eyes and let a friend lead you a few steps. Then thank Jesus for your eyes.

pages.title: Cain and Abel
retelling: Adam and Eve had two sons. Cain grew crops. Abel looked after sheep.
Each brother brought a gift to God. God was pleased with Abel's gift. Cain was upset. He became very angry.
God spoke to Cain. God said, “Do what is right, and I will be pleased with you.”
But Cain did not listen. He let his anger grow. He did a terrible thing, and his brother Abel died.
God asked Cain, “Where is your brother?” Cain said, “I do not know.” But God knew what had happened. Cain had to leave his home.
Even then, God still cared for Cain. God put a mark on him to keep him safe.
pages.message: When we feel angry, we can talk to God. We can choose to do what is right and be kind.

questions.q: What did Cain and Abel bring to God?
questions.a: Cain brought some of his crops. Abel brought some of his sheep.

questions.q: What did God say to Cain before he did the wrong thing?
questions.a: God told him to do what is right and not to let anger win.

questions.q: When you feel very angry, what can you do? Who can you talk to?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Remind the child they can talk to Jesus, and to a grown-up they trust. Pray together.

pages.try_this: When you feel angry, take three slow breaths. Then whisper a short prayer: “Help me, Jesus.”

pages.title: Elijah and the Gentle Whisper
retelling: Elijah was God's prophet. He had just seen God do great things. Then a queen named Jezebel said she would harm him.
Elijah was scared. He ran far away into the desert. He sat under a bush and felt very tired and sad.
He fell asleep. An angel woke him. The angel gave him bread and water. Elijah ate, and he slept again.
Then Elijah walked for forty days to a mountain. He hid in a cave.
God told him to stand on the mountain. A strong wind blew. The ground shook. A fire burned. But God was not in those things.
Then Elijah heard a gentle whisper. It was God's quiet voice. God told Elijah he was not alone. God gave him a new job to do.
pages.message: God cares for us when we are tired and afraid. He can speak to us in a quiet voice.

questions.q: Why did Elijah run away?
questions.a: He was afraid of Queen Jezebel.

questions.q: What did the angel give Elijah?
questions.a: Bread and water, and time to rest.

questions.q: Elijah felt scared and alone. When do you feel that way? You can tell Jesus about it.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share, then remind them God is near and listens. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Sit very quietly for one minute. Listen. Then say, “Thank you, God, that you are near.”

pages.title: Elijah Fed by Ravens
retelling: Elijah was a prophet of God. He told the king that no rain would fall for a long time.
God told Elijah to hide by a little stream. God said, “Ravens will bring you food.”
Elijah did what God said. Every morning and evening, ravens brought him bread and meat. Elijah drank from the stream.
Then the stream dried up. God sent Elijah to a town to meet a poor widow.
She had only a little flour and oil. Elijah said, “God says your flour and oil will not run out.” She shared her food with him.
And God kept his promise. There was enough food every day.
pages.message: God takes care of us in surprising ways. We can trust him for what we need each day. He made everything and takes care of everything, even the birds

questions.q: Who brought Elijah his food at the stream?
questions.a: Ravens, the big black birds.

questions.q: What did the poor widow share with Elijah?
questions.a: A little bread made from her last flour and oil.

questions.q: God gives us food and many other good things. What are you thankful for today? Tell Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name things, then thank God together.

pages.try_this: At your next meal, say thank you to God. Then share something with someone who needs it.

pages.title: Elijah Taken Up in a Fiery Chariot
retelling: Elijah was God's prophet. His helper was a man named Elisha. They walked together.
God was about to take Elijah up to heaven. Elijah said, “Stay here, Elisha.” But Elisha said, “No! I will not leave you.”
They came to the river Jordan. Elijah rolled up his cloak and hit the water. The water split in two! They walked across on dry ground.
Elijah asked, “What can I do for you?” Elisha said, “Please give me a double share of God's Spirit.”
Suddenly a chariot and horses of fire came down. They went between the two men. Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elisha picked up Elijah's cloak. He hit the water, and it split again. God was with Elisha too.
pages.message: God is with his helpers. When one person's work ends, God helps the next one carry on.

questions.q: What did Elijah do to the river with his cloak?
questions.a: He hit the water, and it split so they could cross.

questions.q: What did Elisha ask for?
questions.a: A double share of God's Spirit.

questions.q: Elisha stayed close to Elijah. Who helps you learn about God? You can thank Jesus for them.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child talk about parents, teachers, or friends. Thank God for them together.

pages.try_this: Think of someone who teaches you about God. Say thank you to them this week.

pages.title: Elisha and the Widow's Oil
retelling: A woman was very sad and worried. Her husband had died. She owed money to a man. He was going to take her two sons away.
She asked God's prophet Elisha for help. Elisha asked, “What do you have in your house?” She said, “Only a little jar of oil.”
Elisha said, “Ask your neighbors for empty jars. Get as many as you can.”
She shut the door with her sons. She poured oil from her little jar into the empty jars. The oil kept coming!
When all the jars were full, she asked for one more. But there were no more jars. Then the oil stopped.
Elisha said, “Sell the oil and pay what you owe.” God took care of the woman and her sons.
pages.message: God can use what little we have. When we trust him, he takes care of us.

questions.q: What did the woman have in her house?
questions.a: Just one small jar of oil.

questions.q: What did Elisha tell her to do?
questions.a: To borrow lots of empty jars and fill them with oil.

questions.q: The woman had very little, but God gave her enough. What do you need? You can ask God.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together and thank God for what he gives.

pages.try_this: Put a small cup next to a big bowl. Pour water from one into the other, and thank God for enough.

pages.title: Esther Becomes Queen
retelling: Long ago, a king named Xerxes needed a new queen. He wanted a kind and good woman.
A young woman named Esther lived in his city. She was Jewish. Her parents had died, so her cousin Mordecai took care of her.
Esther was taken to the king's palace. A kind man named Hegai helped her. Esther listened to his advice and was polite to everyone.
Mordecai had told Esther not to share that she was Jewish. Esther did what he said. He checked on her every day.
The king met all the young women. He liked Esther most. He put a crown on her head. Esther was now the queen!
Later, Mordecai heard about a bad plan to hurt the king. He told Esther, and she told the king. The king was safe.
pages.message: God can use quiet, kind people. Esther was ready when God had a job for her.

questions.q: Who took care of Esther when her parents died?
questions.a: Her cousin Mordecai.

questions.q: How did Esther act at the palace?
questions.a: She listened well and was polite and kind to everyone.

questions.q: God put Esther in the palace for a reason. How can you be kind where you are? Ask Jesus to help.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child think of home or school. Pray together for kindness.

pages.try_this: Do one kind thing quietly today. Do not tell anyone. Thank God for the chance.

pages.title: Jacob and Esau's Birthright
retelling: Isaac and Rebekah had twin boys. They were named Esau and Jacob. Esau was born first.
Esau grew up to be a hunter. He loved the outdoors. Jacob liked to stay near the tents.
One day Esau came home from hunting. He was very, very hungry! Jacob was cooking red lentil stew.
Esau said, “Give me some stew now!” Jacob said, “First, sell me your birthright.” A birthright was something special for the oldest son.
Esau said, “I am so hungry. What good is my birthright?” So he gave it away for a bowl of lentil stew. (A type of bean)
Esau ate and left. He did not care about his special place. That was a sad choice and not wise at all.
pages.message: Some things are much more special than a snack. Think before you choose.

questions.q: What did Esau trade for a bowl of lentil stew?
questions.a: His birthright, his special place as the oldest son.

questions.q: Why did Esau make that choice?
questions.a: He was very hungry and wanted food right away.

questions.q: Have you ever wanted something so much that you did not think? You can ask Jesus for help to wait.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray for patience together.

pages.try_this: Next time you feel “I want it now,” count to ten. Then ask God to help you choose well.

pages.title: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
retelling: Jacob was traveling far from home. He was alone. When night came, he found a stone to use as a pillow, and he lay down to sleep.
Jacob had a dream. He saw a tall stairway from the earth to heaven. Angels of God were walking up and down.
God stood above the stairway. God said, “I am with you. I will take care of you wherever you go. I will bring you home.”
Jacob woke up. He said, “God is here, and I did not know it!” He felt amazed and a little afraid.
In the morning Jacob set up his stone pillow. He poured oil on it to show it was special. He named the place Bethel, which means House of God.
Jacob made a promise to God. He said, “You will be my God.”
pages.message: God is with us everywhere, even when we feel alone.

questions.q: What did Jacob use for a pillow?
questions.a: A stone.

questions.q: What did Jacob see in his dream?
questions.a: A stairway to heaven with angels going up and down.

questions.q: Jacob felt alone, but God was with him. When do you feel alone? You can talk to Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Remind them Jesus is always with them, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Before you go to sleep tonight, say, “God, I know you are with me.”

pages.title: Jairus' Daughter
retelling: A man named Jairus came to Jesus. His little girl was very sick. He fell down at the feet of Jesus.
Jairus said, “Please come and help my daughter.” Jesus went with him.
On the way, some people ran up. They said, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble Jesus anymore.”
But Jesus heard them. He told Jairus, “Don't be afraid. Only believe.”
At the house many people were crying. Jesus said, “The girl is only asleep.” Some people laughed.
Jesus went in with the girl's mother and father. He took her hand. He said, “Little girl, get up!” She stood up and walked! Jesus said, “Give her something to eat.”
pages.message: Jesus is stronger than anything that scares us. We can trust him.

questions.q: What did Jairus ask Jesus to do?
questions.a: To come and help his sick daughter.

questions.q: What did Jesus say to Jairus when the people said she had died?
questions.a: “Do not be afraid. Just believe.”

questions.q: Jairus was afraid, but Jesus helped him. What makes you afraid? You can tell Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together and remind them Jesus is stronger than fear.

pages.try_this: Draw a picture of Jesus holding a child's hand. Say thank you for his care.

pages.title: Jesus Blesses the Children
retelling: Some moms and dads brought their children to Jesus. They wanted Jesus to bless them.
Jesus' friends said, “Stop! Do not bother Jesus.” But Jesus was not happy about that.
Jesus said, “Let the children come to me. Do not stop them!”
Jesus took the children in his arms. He put his hands on them. He blessed each one.
Jesus loves children very much. He loves you!
pages.message: Jesus loves children. He is glad when we come to him.

questions.q: Who came to see Jesus?
questions.a: Children, and their parents.

questions.q: What did Jesus do for the children?
questions.a: He hugged them and blessed them.

questions.q: Jesus loves you. How can you say thank you to him?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer. Say a thank-you prayer together.

pages.try_this: Give someone a big hug today. Say, “Jesus loves you.”

pages.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
retelling: Jesus was eating a special meal with his twelve friends. It was nearly time for him to go back to his Father.
In those days, people's feet got dusty from walking. A servant usually washed them. But no servant was there.
Jesus got up. He wrapped a towel around his waist. He poured water in a bowl. Then he began to wash his friends' feet!
Peter said, “Lord, you should not wash my feet!” Jesus said, “If I do not wash you, you cannot be part of my family.” Peter said, “Then wash my hands and head too!”
When Jesus finished, he sat down. He said, “I am your teacher and Lord. I washed your feet. Now you should help one another.”
pages.message: Jesus shows us how to love. We can help others, even in small ways.

questions.q: What did Jesus do for his friends?
questions.a: He washed their feet.

questions.q: Why did Jesus wash their feet?
questions.a: To show them how to serve and love one another.

questions.q: How can you help someone this week? You can ask Jesus to show you.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child think of ideas, like helping at home. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Do a job for someone without being asked. It could be putting away dishes or shoes.

pages.title: Joshua and the Sun Standing Still
retelling: Joshua was the leader of God's people. The people of Gibeon were his friends. Five kings came to attack them.
The Gibeonites sent a message. “Please come and help us!” Joshua walked all night to reach them.
God said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid. I will help you win.”
The battle began. God sent big hailstones from the sky. Many enemies ran away.
Joshua needed more daylight to finish the fight. He prayed to God in front of everyone. He said, “Sun, stand still!”
And the sun stayed in the sky! God had listened to Joshua. God's people won the battle.
pages.message: God hears our prayers. We can ask him for help, and he is always stronger than any enemy.

questions.q: Who asked Joshua for help?
questions.a: The people of Gibeon.

questions.q: What did Joshua ask God to do?
questions.a: To make the sun stand still.

questions.q: Joshua asked God for help. What can you ask God for today?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child choose. Pray together and thank God for hearing.

pages.try_this: Look at the sun or sky today. Say, “Thank you, God, for the sun. You are in charge.”

pages.title: Naaman Healed of Leprosy
retelling: Naaman was a brave army leader. But he had a skin disease called leprosy. It was very hard for him.
A young girl worked in his home. She had been taken from her own country. She said, “A prophet in Israel can heal you.”
Naaman went to the prophet Elisha with his horses and chariots. Elisha did not come out. He sent a message: “Wash in the river Jordan seven times.”
Naaman was angry. “I thought he would wave his hand! The rivers at home are better!” He turned to leave.
His servants said, “Please try it. It is not hard.” So Naaman went down into the river. He dipped seven times.
His skin became healthy like a child's! Naaman said, “Now I know there is only one true God.”
pages.message: God can heal, and he can use anyone. When God says something, it is best to listen.

questions.q: Who told Naaman about the prophet?
questions.a: A young girl who worked in his home.

questions.q: What did Elisha tell Naaman to do?
questions.a: To wash in the Jordan River seven times.

questions.q: Naaman did not want to do it at first. Is it hard for you to listen sometimes? Ask Jesus to help you.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together for a listening heart.

pages.try_this: Count to seven out loud as you wash your hands. Thank God for water and for healing.

pages.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream
retelling: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had a strange dream. It troubled him so much that he could not sleep.
He called his wise men. “Tell me my dream and what it means!” They said, “No one can do that.” The king was furious.
Daniel heard about it. He asked for time. He and his friends prayed to God, “Please show us the secret.”
That night God showed Daniel the dream. Daniel praised God. “Wisdom and power belong to God.”

Daniel told the king about a huge statue. It had a gold head, silver arms, bronze belly, iron legs and feet of iron and clay. A rock hit the statue, and it fell to pieces. Then the rock grew into a mountain.
Daniel said, “Only God can explain this. God's kingdom will last forever.” The king bowed down and said, “Your God is great.”
pages.message: God knows the future. Kings come and go, but God's kingdom lasts forever.

questions.q: What did the king dream about?
questions.a: A huge statue made of different metals.

questions.q: Who told the king what the dream meant?
questions.a: Daniel, with God's help.

questions.q: Daniel prayed when he had a problem. What can you pray about? You can talk to God now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Draw the statue from the dream. Write on it, “God's kingdom lasts forever.”
pages.doctrine_note: Christians understand the kingdoms in this dream, and how it relates to the end times and to the kingdom of God, in different ways. This page says only what the text says.

pages.title: Paul and Silas in Prison
retelling: Paul and Silas were friends of Jesus. They told people the good news about him in a city called Philippi.
Some angry men grabbed them. They were beaten. Then Paul and Silas were put in jail. Their feet were locked in heavy blocks.
Late at night, Paul and Silas were praying. They were singing songs to God. The other prisoners were listening.
Suddenly there was a big earthquake! The doors flew open. Everyone's chains fell off.
The jailer woke up. He was very afraid. He thought the prisoners had run away. But Paul called, “We are all here!”
The jailer asked, “What must I do to be saved?” Paul said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus.” The jailer and his family believed, and they were all very happy.
pages.message: We can sing and pray to God even when things are hard. God can do wonderful things.

questions.q: What did Paul and Silas do in jail at midnight?
questions.a: They prayed and sang songs to God.

questions.q: What happened when the earthquake came?
questions.a: The doors opened and the chains fell off.

questions.q: Paul and Silas sang when things were hard. What song makes you happy? You can sing it to Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name a song. Sing it together.

pages.try_this: Sing your favorite song about Jesus out loud. Sing it to someone who feels sad.

pages.title: Rahab and the Spies of Jericho
retelling: God's people were about to enter a new land. Joshua sent two spies to look at the city of Jericho.
The spies went to the house of a woman named Rahab. She had heard about God. She knew God was powerful.
The king of Jericho heard about the spies. He sent soldiers to find them. But Rahab hid the spies on her roof, under some stalks.
She told the soldiers, “The men went away. Hurry, you can catch them!” The soldiers left.
Rahab said to the spies, “Please keep my family safe.” They said, “Tie a red rope in your window. We will remember.”
Rahab let the spies down by a rope from her window. They escaped. And Rahab trusted God.
pages.message: God cares for people who trust him. Rahab believed in God, and he kept her family safe.

questions.q: Where did Rahab hide the spies?
questions.a: On her roof, under stalks of flax.

questions.q: What did Rahab tie in her window?
questions.a: A red rope, as a sign to keep her family safe.

questions.q: Rahab was brave. When is it hard to be brave? You can ask Jesus to help you.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together for courage.

pages.try_this: Tie a red ribbon somewhere you will see it. Remember that God keeps those who trust him.

pages.title: Samson and Delilah
retelling: Samson was a very strong man. God gave him his strength. His long hair was a sign of a special promise to God.
Some enemies wanted to find the secret of his strength. A woman named Delilah kept asking Samson, “Tell me your secret.”
At first Samson did not tell the truth. But Delilah asked again and again. At last, Samson told her. “If my hair is cut, I will lose my strength.”
His enemies cut his hair. Samson became weak. They took him away.
Samson felt so sorry. His hair began to grow back. He prayed, “God, please make me strong once more.”
God heard Samson's prayer. He helped Samson one last time.
pages.message: Our strength comes from God. If we make a mistake, we can pray and God still hears us.

questions.q: What was the secret of Samson's strength?
questions.a: God gave him strength, and his long hair was a sign of his promise to God.

questions.q: What did Samson do when he was weak and sorry?
questions.a: He prayed to God for help.

questions.q: Everyone makes mistakes. What can we do when we feel sorry? You can tell Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Remind the child that Jesus forgives. Pray together.

pages.try_this: If you have said sorry to God lately, thank him that he forgives. If not, tell him now.

pages.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
retelling: Solomon became king when he was young. He loved God and wanted to lead well.
One night God spoke to him in a dream. God said, “Ask for anything. I will give it to you.”
Solomon could have asked for money or a long life. But he said, “Please give me a wise and listening heart so I can help your people.”
God was very happy with this answer. God said, “I will make you the wisest person ever. And I will give you riches too.”
One day two mothers came to Solomon. Both said a baby was theirs. Solomon needed to find the real mother.
Solomon wisely saw which mother truly loved the baby. The people were amazed. They saw that God had made him wise.
pages.message: God gives wisdom to anyone who asks. We can ask for wisdom, too.

questions.q: What did Solomon ask God for?
questions.a: A wise and listening heart.

questions.q: How did God answer?
questions.a: God gave Solomon wisdom and also riches.

questions.q: If God said, “Ask for anything,” what would you ask for? You can talk to Jesus about it.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer. Talk about asking God for wisdom, and pray together.

pages.try_this: Ask God for wisdom before a big choice this week. Say, “Please help me choose well.”

pages.title: Spies Sent into Canaan
retelling: God's people were near a new land. It was called Canaan. Moses sent twelve men to look at it.
The twelve men walked all around for forty days. They saw big cities. They saw wonderful fruit. They carried back one huge bunch of grapes!
They said, “The land is rich. But the people are big and strong. Their cities have tall walls.”
Ten of the spies were afraid. They said, “We looked like little grasshoppers!” But Caleb and Joshua said, “God is with us! We can do it!”
The people listened to the ten. They were scared and cried all night. They did not trust God.
So God's people had to wait many years. Caleb and Joshua trusted God, and they got to enter the land.
pages.message: God is bigger than anything we fear. When we trust him, we can be brave.

questions.q: How many spies went to look at the land?
questions.a: Twelve.

questions.q: What did Caleb and Joshua say?
questions.a: That God was with them and they could do it.

questions.q: The people were scared. What scares you? You can tell Jesus about it.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Remind them God is bigger than fear. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Pick one scary thing. Say out loud, “God is bigger than this.” Say it again.

pages.title: The Boy Jesus in the Temple
retelling: Every year, Mary and Joseph went to Jerusalem for a special feast. When Jesus was twelve, he went too.
After the feast, the family walked home with many friends and relatives. Mary and Joseph thought Jesus was with them.
But Jesus was not there! They looked for him all around. Mary and Joseph were very worried. They went back to Jerusalem.
After three days, they found Jesus. He was at the temple, sitting with the teachers. He was listening and asking questions. Everyone was amazed at how much he knew.
Mary said, “We were so worried!” Jesus said, “Why were you looking for me? I needed to be at my Father's house.”
Then Jesus went home with them. He obeyed Mary and Joseph. And Jesus kept growing wiser and stronger.
pages.message: Jesus loved his Father and his family. We can learn and grow too.

questions.q: Where did Mary and Joseph find Jesus?
questions.a: In the temple, with the teachers.

questions.q: What was Jesus doing there?
questions.a: Listening and asking questions.

questions.q: Jesus asked good questions. What would you like to ask God? You can talk to him now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child ask. Say that God loves our questions. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Ask a grown-up a good question about the Bible today. Listen to the answer.

pages.title: The Crucifixion of Jesus
retelling: Jesus had been arrested and treated unfairly. The soldiers made fun of him. They put a crown of thorns on his head. They led him out to be crucified.
Jesus carried his own cross and later a  man named Simon was made to carry Jesus' cross. At a place called Golgotha, Jesus was put on the cross.
Above him was a sign that said, “The King of the Jews.” People made fun of him. Some said, “Save yourself!”
At noon, the sky became dark for three hours. Then Jesus cried out in a loud voice. He breathed his last breath.
At that moment, the big curtain in the temple tore in two, from top to bottom.
A Roman officer was standing near. He saw how Jesus died. He said, “This man really was God's Son!” Some women who loved Jesus watched from far away.
pages.message: Jesus loved us so much that he gave his life for us. His love is bigger than we can imagine.

questions.q: What did the sign above Jesus say?
questions.a: “The King of the Jews.”

questions.q: What happened to the curtain in the temple?
questions.a: It tore in two, from top to bottom.

questions.q: Jesus died because he loves us. How can you thank him? You can tell him now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer gently. Remind them that Jesus rose again. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Make a small cross from sticks or paper. Put it where you will see it and remember Jesus' love.

pages.title: The Fiery Furnace
retelling: King Nebuchadnezzar made a huge gold statue. He said, “Everyone must bow down to it when the music plays.”
Three friends, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, would not bow. They said, “We will only worship God.”
The king was very angry. He said, “I will throw you into the hot furnace!” The friends said, “Our God can save us. But even if he does not, we will not bow to your statue.”
The king ordered the fire made hotter. The three friends were tied up and thrown in.
Then the king jumped up. “I see four men walking in the fire! They are not hurt. The fourth one looks like a heavenly being.”
The friends came out. Not even their clothes smelled like smoke! The king said, “Praise their God!”
pages.message: God is with us when we trust him. We can choose to do right, even when it is hard.

questions.q: Why would the three friends not bow down?
questions.a: They only wanted to worship God.

questions.q: Who was in the fire with them?
questions.a: A fourth person, who looked like a son of the gods.

questions.q: The friends were brave. When is it hard to do the right thing? You can ask Jesus to help.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together for courage.

pages.try_this: Stand up straight and say, “I will worship God only.” Then ask God to help you be brave.

pages.title: The First Passover
retelling: God's people were slaves in Egypt. God was going to set them free. First, God gave Moses special instructions.
Each family had to choose a lamb. It had to be a healthy lamb with no marks.
The families put some of the lamb's blood on their doorposts. Then they ate a meal together. They had flat bread and bitter herbs.
They ate in a hurry. They were ready to go on a trip. They had their shoes on and their walking sticks in their hands.
God said, “When I see the blood on your door, I will pass over your house. You will be safe.”
God told his people to remember this night every year. We call it Passover.
pages.message: God keeps his people safe. The Passover lamb makes us think of Jesus, the Lamb of God.

questions.q: What did the families put on their doors?
questions.a: Blood from the lamb.

questions.q: Why did God ask them to eat in a hurry?
questions.a: They were about to leave Egypt and be free.

questions.q: The lamb reminds us of Jesus. How did Jesus take care of us? You can thank him.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer. Say that Jesus is our Lamb and thank him together.

pages.try_this: Draw a red mark on a paper door. Say, “Thank you, Jesus, for keeping me safe.”

pages.title: The Golden Calf
retelling: Moses went up a mountain to talk to God. He was gone for a long time.
The people got tired of waiting. They said to Aaron, “Make us a god we can see!”
Aaron asked them for their gold earrings. He melted the gold and made a calf. The people said, “This is our god!”
God was sad. He told Moses what the people had done. Moses prayed, “Please, God, forgive them.”
God listened to Moses. He did not punish the people the way he said.
Moses came down the mountain. He saw what the people had made. He felt very upset and breaks the tablets. God had to write down the law again on new Tablets.
pages.message: Only God deserves our worship. If we say sorry, God listens.

questions.q: What did the people make while Moses was away?
questions.a: A golden calf.

questions.q: What did Moses do when God was sad?
questions.a: He prayed for the people.

questions.q: The people did not wait for God. When is it hard to wait? You can tell Jesus.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together for patience and trust.

pages.try_this: Think of something you love a lot. Tell God, “You are more important than anything.”

pages.title: The Handwriting on the Wall
retelling: King Belshazzar gave a huge party for a thousand people. He ordered the gold cups from God's temple to be brought out. They drank wine from them and praised false gods.
Suddenly a hand appeared. It wrote strange words on the palace wall. The king turned pale, and his knees shook.
None of his wise men could read the words. The queen remembered Daniel. “He can explain it,” she said.
Daniel told the king, “God made your grandfather great. But he became proud, and God made him humble. You knew this, but you still did not honor God.”
Daniel read the words. He said, “God has counted your days. You have been weighed and found lacking. Your kingdom will be given to others.”
That very night, the kingdom did change hands.
pages.message: Pride leads to a fall. We should honor God and treat holy things with respect.

questions.q: What did Belshazzar do with the cups from God's temple?
questions.a: He used them at his party to praise false gods.

questions.q: Who could read the writing?
questions.a: Daniel.

questions.q: Belshazzar knew about God but ignored him. How can we honor God each day? Ask Jesus to help.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer. Pray together for a humble heart.

pages.try_this: Write one thing on paper that you can do each day to honor God. Put it on your wall.

pages.title: The Last Supper
retelling: It was the time of Passover. Jesus sent two of his friends to get a room ready. He told them, “A man with a water jug will show you the place.” Everything happened just as he said.
That evening Jesus sat at the table with his twelve friends. He said, “I have wanted so much to eat this meal with you before I suffer.”
Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke it and gave it to them. “This is my body, given for you. Remember me when you eat it.”
After the meal, he took a cup. He said, “This cup is a new promise from God. It is made with my blood.”
Then Jesus said sadly, “One of you will turn against me.” The friends were shocked. They asked each other who it could be.
pages.message: Jesus wanted his friends to remember him. We remember what he did for us when we share the bread and the cup.

questions.q: What did Jesus do with the bread?
questions.a: He thanked God, broke it and gave it to his friends.

questions.q: What did Jesus ask his friends to do?
questions.a: To remember him.

questions.q: Jesus wanted his friends to remember him. What do you want to remember about Jesus?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Thank Jesus together for what he has done.

pages.try_this: At your next meal, pause and say, “Jesus, thank you for loving me.”
pages.doctrine_note: Christians keep this meal with different names, such as the Lord's Supper, Communion or the Eucharist, and understand the bread and the cup in different ways. This page says only what the text says.

pages.title: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
retelling: Jesus told a story. A shepherd had one hundred sheep. One sheep ran away.
The shepherd left the ninety-nine sheep safe in the field. He went to look for the lost sheep.
He looked and looked. At last, he found it! He put the sheep on his shoulders and carried it home. He called his friends, “Let's celebrate! I found my lost sheep!”
Then Jesus told another story. A woman had ten coins. She lost one.
She lit a lamp and swept the house. She searched and searched. When she found the coin, she was so happy! She told her friends.
Jesus said, “That is how God feels when one person comes back to him. All heaven celebrates!”
pages.message: God loves every one of us. He is happy when someone who is lost is found.

questions.q: What did the shepherd do when he lost a sheep?
questions.a: He went to look for it until he found it.

questions.q: How did the woman feel when she found her coin?
questions.a: Very happy. She called her friends.

questions.q: Jesus loves it when people come to him. How can you tell him you love him?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer. Pray a thank-you prayer together.

pages.try_this: Hide a small coin and look for it with a friend. When you find it, say, “God finds us too!”

pages.title: The Parable of the Talents
retelling: Jesus told a story about a man who was going on a trip. He called three servants. He gave them each some money to look after.
To the first, he gave five bags of money. To the second, two. To the third, one.
The first servant used his money well. He made five more bags. The second servant did too. He made two more.
But the third servant was afraid. He dug a hole and hid the money in the ground.
When the man came home, he was happy with the first two. He said, “Well done! You did a good job.”
He was not happy with the third. He said, “You should have tried.” Jesus wants us to use what we have for him.
pages.message: God gives each of us gifts. When we use them well, God is pleased.

questions.q: How many servants were there?
questions.a: Three.

questions.q: What did the third servant do with his money?
questions.a: He hid it in the ground.

questions.q: What are you good at? You can ask Jesus to show you how to use it to help others.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name something. Pray together and thank God for gifts.

pages.try_this: Use something you are good at to help someone this week. Draw, sing, build, or share.

pages.title: The Ten Commandments at Sinai
retelling: God had just rescued his people from slavery in Egypt. Now they were camped at Mount Sinai. God spoke to them from the mountain.
God said, “I rescued you. Here is how to live in my way.” These are the Ten Commandments.
The first commands are about loving God. Worship only God. Do not make idols. Respect God's name. Keep the Sabbath as a day of rest.
The other commands are about loving people. Honor your father and mother. Do not hurt others. Be faithful. Do not steal. Do not tell lies. Do not be jealous of what other people have.
The people saw thunder and lightning on the mountain. They were afraid. They stood far away.
God gave these laws to help his people live well and know him.
pages.message: God's rules are a gift. They show us how to love God and love people.

questions.q: What did God do for his people before he gave the Commandments?
questions.a: He rescued them from slavery in Egypt.

questions.q: What are the first commands about?
questions.a: Loving God.

questions.q: Which commandment is hard for you? You can ask Jesus to help you.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share honestly. Remind them that Jesus helps and forgives. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Pick one commandment to practice this week. Ask God to help you every day.
pages.doctrine_note: Christians number the commandments in different ways, and understand the Sabbath and the place of the law in Christian life in different ways. This page says only what the text says.

pages.title: The Ten Lepers
retelling: One day Jesus was walking into a village. Ten men were standing far away. They had a sickness called leprosy.
They shouted, “Jesus! Please help us!” Jesus said, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.”
As they were on their way, something wonderful happened. They were all healed! Their skin was clean.
One man came back. He was so thankful. He fell at Jesus' feet and said thank you in a loud voice. This man was from Samaria.
Jesus asked, “Were not ten healed? Where are the other nine?” Then Jesus said to the man, “Get up. Your faith has made you well.”
pages.message: Saying thank you to God is important. Jesus loves a thankful heart.

questions.q: How many men did Jesus heal?
questions.a: Ten.

questions.q: How many came back to say thank you?
questions.a: Only one.

questions.q: What are you thankful for? You can thank Jesus now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child name things. Say a thank-you prayer together.

pages.try_this: Write a thank-you note to someone. Then say thank you to God out loud.

pages.title: The Ten Plagues of Egypt
retelling: God's people were slaves in Egypt. God sent Moses and Aaron to speak to the king, called Pharaoh. They said, “Let God's people go.”
Pharaoh said no. So God sent ten plagues, one after another. The first was that the river turned to blood.
Then came frogs, gnats and flies. After that, the animals got sick, and people got sores. Then hail fell, locusts came, and darkness covered the land.
Pharaoh said he would let the people go. Then he changed his mind again and again. His heart was hard.
In the land of Goshen, where God's people lived, God kept them safe from many plagues.
The last plague was the saddest. After it, Pharaoh told God's people to leave.
pages.message: God is stronger than any king. He hears his people and sets them free.

questions.q: What was the first plague?
questions.a: The river turned to blood.

questions.q: What did Pharaoh do each time the plague stopped?
questions.a: He changed his mind and would not let the people go.

questions.q: God heard his people when they were in trouble. What can you talk to God about? You can pray now.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together and thank God for hearing.

pages.try_this: Count the plagues on your fingers. Say, “God is stronger than anything.”
pages.doctrine_note: Christians understand how God hardened Pharaoh's heart, and how that relates to Pharaoh's own choices, in different ways. This page says only what the text says.

pages.title: The Tower of Babel
retelling: Long ago, all the people in the world spoke one language. They moved to a flat valley and made their home there.
The people said, “Let's build a city! Let's build a tower to the sky!” They made bricks and baked them hard.
They said, “We will be famous. Everyone will know us.” They wanted to be great without God.
God looked down. He saw their plans. God knew they were proud.
So God mixed up their languages. Now they could not understand each other. They had to stop building.
The people spread out all over the earth. The city was named Babel.
pages.message: God is greater than anything we build. We should give God the honor.

questions.q: What were the people building?
