questions.a: A city and a tall tower.

questions.q: What did God do to their words?
questions.a: He mixed up their languages.

questions.q: The people wanted to be famous. What can we do to give God honor?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child think. Talk about thanking God and being kind. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Build a tower of blocks. Then say, “God, you are greater than anything I can build.”

pages.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
retelling: God's Spirit took Ezekiel to a valley. It was full of old, dry bones. They covered the ground.
God asked, “Can these bones live again?” Ezekiel said, “Lord, only you know.”
God said, “Speak to the bones. Tell them to hear my words.” Ezekiel did. There was a loud rattling sound. The bones came together!
Then muscles and skin covered the bones. But the bodies had no breath. God told Ezekiel to call for the breath.
Ezekiel spoke again. Breath came into the bodies. They stood up. It was a huge army!
God said, “The bones are my people. They think they have no hope. But I will give them my Spirit and new life.”
pages.message: God brings new life when it seems there is no hope. His Spirit gives life.

questions.q: What did God show Ezekiel?
questions.a: A valley full of dry bones that came to life.

questions.q: What did the bones stand for?
questions.a: God's people, who felt they had no hope.

questions.q: God can bring life where there seems to be none. When do you feel hopeless? You can pray.
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child share. Pray together for hope.

pages.try_this: Write “HOPE” on a paper. Put it where you can see it. Thank God for giving new life.
pages.doctrine_note: Christians understand this vision, including how it relates to the restoration of Israel and to the resurrection of the dead, in different ways. This page says only what the text says.

pages.title: The Visit of the Wise Men
retelling: Some wise men lived far away. They saw a bright new star. They knew it was a sign for a new king.
They followed the star. It was a long trip. They came to a king named Herod. “Where is the baby king?” they asked.
The star led them to Bethlehem. It stopped over a house. They went in and saw the little child Jesus with his mother, Mary.
They bowed down and worshiped Jesus. They gave him gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh.
God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod. So they went home a new way.
pages.message: People came from far away to worship Jesus. We can worship him too.

questions.q: What did the wise men follow?
questions.a: A bright star.

questions.q: What gifts did they bring Jesus?
questions.a: Gold, frankincense and myrrh.

questions.q: The wise men gave gifts to Jesus. What can you give Jesus?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child answer, like love, songs or kindness. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Make a card for Jesus. Draw a star on it. Say thank you for sending Jesus.

pages.title: The Widow's Offering
retelling: Jesus sat near the place in the temple where people gave money. He watched as people put in their gifts.
Rich people came. They put in a lot of money. The coins made a loud clink.
Then a poor widow came. She put in two tiny coins. They were worth very little.
Jesus called his friends. He said, “This poor woman gave more than all the others!”
The rich people gave only part of what they had. But the widow gave all she had. She trusted God to take care of her.
pages.message: God loves a cheerful giver. A small gift given with love is special to him.

questions.q: What did the poor widow give?
questions.a: Two tiny coins.

questions.q: Why did Jesus say her gift was more?
questions.a: She gave all she had, and she trusted God.

questions.q: What can you give to God, even if you have only a little?
questions.a: There is no wrong answer. Let the child think about time, kindness and coins. Pray together.

pages.try_this: Put a few coins in a jar. Give it to someone in need, or put it in a church offering.
